Who makes good ammo for 38 p? I'm looking at hollow point for home defense.

Hollow points are good, but they're expensive when you compare them to FMJ target loads.

Personally, I shoot Winchester White Box or Federals, all FMJ, at the range. This way I don't shoot up my expensive hollow point ammo. Of course, I'll put some hollow points down rance every once in a while, since every gun is going to act differently with different types of ammo, but the majority of my shooting is always with cheaper target loads.

For self defense ammo, I honestly can't give you all of the details in a Voat comment... There's just so much to consider. You have Hydroshocks, jacketed hollow points, bonded hollow points, Hornady ballistic tips... The list just goes on and on... I'd recommend you watch some YouTube videos (I've found tnoutdoors9 entertaining, educational, and thorough), and find one that you can shoot well, that isn't too snappy in that smaller revolver.

I'm a stickler for BHP rounds, because I want the added penetration and I want to avoid jacket separation... Both of which can turn bad if you don't have a BHP and you have to shoot through things, like a car windshield. So I usually stick with Speer Gold Dots or Winchester PDX1 ammo.

But, if I can't get those, my backup is always Hornady with their ballistic tips or Winchester Rangers. The ballistic "plug" tips on the Hornady rounds assure the hollow point doesn't clog, so you get good expansion from the bullet... And the Rangers have sharp teeth folded into the hollow point, which expand and rotate with the twist of the slug, which does some pretty wicked damage.

But, again, that's all my personal preference... You ask 100 people what they prefer and you'll probably get 100 different answers. I say watch some videos, try out a couple of different types of ammunition and find what you like and can shoot well... Remember, if you can' t handle a higher pressure round, don't use it and go with a lower pressure round... You can't miss enough to kill a bad guy... Don't let anyone belittle you for your caliber choice, round choice, or gun choice... All of these calibers will kill you if used correctly.

I'd, again, invest HEAVILY in some FMJ target ammo and just spend some time in a friend's back yard or on a range, and put rounds through your new toy. That's the only way to get proficient with it. Remember: there's two ways of practicing... Practicing until you can get it right, and practicing until you can't get it wrong... And there's a WORLD of difference between the two.

Also, since Hickok45 was on the front page recently, and we're talking about YouTube videos: you should also check out his video about holding a revolver correctly! There's a wrong way to hold it, which can actually hurt you pretty badly. You'll want to avoid that at all costs.
